chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Jews asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'Describe for us the lineage of your Lord.' So he waited three (days) without answering them. Then it was revealed:
'Say: He, Allah, is One' — to the end of it.
And it was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub.

key_terms.انسب: Describe the lineage/genealogy — a request to provide nasab (lineage), which the Arabs used to define identity and social standing
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He, Allah, is One — the opening of Surah al-Ikhlas (112:1), God's answer to the Jews' challenge
key_terms.لبث: He waited/remained — indicating the Prophet did not answer immediately but waited for divine revelation
key_terms.نزلت: Was revealed — referring to the Quranic revelation as a direct response from God

ai.seo_question: Why was Surah al-Ikhlas (Say He is Allah, One) revealed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the occasion of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for Surah al-Ikhlas (112). The Jews challenged the Prophet by asking him to provide a genealogy or lineage for God — a concept entirely foreign to Islamic theology — as was customary in Arab tribal culture to establish someone's status and identity through ancestry. The Prophet waited three days in contemplation or awaiting divine guidance, after which Surah al-Ikhlas was revealed, affirming God's absolute unity and transcendence beyond any notion of lineage or physical description.
word_analysis: and it was narrated by him
